keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks (its Talpur row is a Gilgit-Baltistan outline after 1843). The area ratio disc/infobox is 0.98, but the disc is not the state's boundary and the page gives no year for the area. The Talpur page says Ali Murad helped the British in 1845 and was later accused of plotting and lost lands in upper Sindh (undated), so the state was probably larger at first; the pages give no figure. Repair 2026-10-25: extended to 1955 with the state's end. The Khairpur District page: '1941 figures are for Khairpur State, which roughly correspond to the present district' (district area 15,910 km2), which supports the infobox area for the late state. The Khairpur (town) page says that after Ali Murad was stripped of his upper-Sindh lands 'the remaining land under his control consisted mostly of Khairpur city, and its immediate environs' (accused 1851-2; no districts, no area): the 1843-1852 state was larger than this disc by an unknown amount, see notes.

region.text: Khairpur, the Talpur branch of upper Sindh, left outside the annexation of Sindh

ledger.note: 1843: Khairpur, whose Mir Ali Murad Talpur Napier had won over, survives the conquest of Sindh as a princely state. The Talpur infobox: Khairpur 'continued in upper Sindh as the Khairpur princely state until 1955: 1843'; the Battle of Miani page: Napier 'had already secured the cooperation of the Amir of Khairpur, Mir Ali Murad Talpur, through promises of land and titles'; the Khairpur infobox: 'Princely state under British Raj (1838-1947)' and 'Established: 1783'. The land is the page's area drawn as a disc. The Mir Ali Murad Khan Talpur page: the treaty of 4 April 1832 'recognised the political individuality of Khairpur' (the state is dated from 1843 only because talpur-dynasty keeps the branch until then, see notes).

30 September 1955: the Khairpur state is disestablished. The page: 'Disestablished: 30 September 1955', status 'Princely state of Pakistan (1947-1955)', 'fully amalgamated into West Pakistan in 1955'. It had acceded to Pakistan on 3 October 1947 and stayed a princely state of Pakistan (a vassal, recorded by islamic-republic-of-pakistan). The page does not mention One Unit; bahawalpur-state and khanate-of-kalat use 14 October 1955.

wars.name: British conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: Napier isolated the Amir of Khairpur before Miani; when the Hyderabad Talpurs fell, Khairpur stayed a princely state.
wars.note: The British conquest page: 'Napier had already successfully isolated the Amir of Khairpur'. Khairpur is not a zone: the fighting was in the Hyderabad district.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary or a survey for Khairpur; the 70 km disc is an approximation of the infobox area (15,730 km2, no year; Khairpur District: 1941 state roughly the present district).

notes:
Written by sa-05-g as a direct counterpart of talpur-dynasty that no Cliopatria row covers. Borders are thin: the only area is the infobox's 15,730 km2 (no year), supported for the late state by the Khairpur District footnote ('1941 figures are for Khairpur State, which roughly correspond to the present district').

Repair 2026-10-25 (reviewer verdict fail): the state now ends at its disestablishment, 30 September 1955 (Khairpur page: 'Princely state of Pakistan (1947-1955)', 'fully amalgamated into West Pakistan in 1955'), not at the accession of 3 October 1947. The 1947 loss to islamic-republic-of-pakistan was deleted: the accession made Khairpur a vassal of Pakistan, which the overlord records (vassal events are overlord-side), and the dissolve at 1955-9 now carries islamic-republic-of-pakistan as counterpart. The page also says 'Conquered by the British in 1843 following the Battle of Miani'; read here as the conquest of Sindh, with Khairpur kept as a princely state.

Open questions. (1) Start: the Khairpur page says 'Established: 1783' (Sohrab Khan); the Talpur page says a British treaty of 1832 recognised Khairpur as independent and the Mir Ali Murad Khan Talpur page dates it 4 April 1832 ('recognised the political individuality of Khairpur'; reign 4 April 1832 - 2 April 1894). The state is dated from 1843 here only because talpur-dynasty keeps the branch until then; whoever revises both may start this dossier in 1832 and cut Khairpur out of the Talpur shape then. (2) Lost lands, not written: the Khairpur (town) page says Ali Murad 'helped the British in 1845-7 during the Turki campaign' but 'was later accused of plotting against the British in 1851-2' and 'was stripped of his lands in upper Sindh by the British East India Company', so that 'the remaining land under his control consisted mostly of Khairpur city, and its immediate environs'. No page opened names the districts or the year of the stripping (Khairpur princely state, Khairpur District, Mir Ali Murad Khan Talpur and the Talpur dynasty page are silent or undated; Ali_Murad_Khan_Talpur does not exist), so no loss event is written: it would take unplaced land from a shape that is itself only a disc of the late state, and the 1843-1852 extent is unknown. Leads only: the Bahawalpur page (Sabzalkot and Bhung given to the Nawab, 1847-48; bahawalpur-state /ledger/1) and the Mir Sohrab Khan Talpur page (he 'captured ... the Sabzal Kot region from the Nawab of Bahawalpur') suggest those districts, but no page opened ties them to Ali Murad and the dates (1847-48 against 1851-2) differ. A gap-filler should try the Sabzalkot, Ghotki District or Kashmore pages. The Talpur page adds that in 1857 Ali Murad protected the Shikarpur jail and treasury and in 1866 the British promised to recognise his successors; neither moves a border. (3) The Miani page says 'Mir Ali Murad Khan Talpur was taken aboard the sloop HMS Nimrod and exiled to Burma' (undated), which cannot be the Khairpur Ali Murad who ruled to 1894; unresolved. (4) The ruler table disagrees with the Talpur page (Rustam 1830-1842 against Ali Murad in 1832) and the infobox gives different dates (Sohrab Khan 1783-1811, George Ali Murad II 1947-1954); the last ruler is entered to 1954 as the infobox says. (5) British suzerainty (infobox 'Princely state under British Raj (1838-1947)') belongs to british-empire and british-raj as a vassal_start/vassal_end with this slug; both draw the whole Sind province as theirs from 1843, which overlaps this state. (6) islamic-republic-of-pakistan has no Khairpur event today (its notes list Khairpur among the states without a dossier and its accession date as unresolved); under the model used here it should record vassal_start khairpur-state 1947-10 and vassal_end 1955-9 and the merger (gain) at 1955-9. Its gains of bahawalpur-state (1947-10) and khanate-of-kalat (1948-3) at accession contradict those two dossiers, which run to 14 October 1955 and dissolve into Pakistan; one model is needed for the princely states of Pakistan. The 30 September 1955 date is the Khairpur page's own; it does not mention One Unit (14 October 1955). The 'Established' dates of Khairpur District (15 October 1955) and of the Khairpur town page (24 October 1955) are district dates and are not used.
